qualifiers.text: For a hundred years, Ren Sato's 1.43-second cube solve has stood untouched. You are Inez, a night-shift supermarket worker with an unusual ability to see several possible solutions at once. At the continental championship, your first attempts are slow and your hands begin to shake.

choices.text: Call your mother, who reminds you that the supermarket will still be there tomorrow
Watch Ren's old recording and study the moment after the solve

text.value: Your mother's voice stays with you as the finalists take their places. Your coach says to stop searching for the perfect solve and decide sooner. The scramble appears on the screen.
Ren's face stays in your mind: after setting the record, she looked uncertain too. You stop trying to imitate her hands and study the scramble on your own terms.

choices.text: Choose the reliable solution you have practiced for months
Choose the unfamiliar, shorter path and trust your hands

the_timer.text: You solve, and the cube lands on the mat. The timer displays 1.42. Officials review the scramble, the cube, the video, and your hands. For forty-three minutes, nobody tells you whether a century has ended.

choices.text: Wait with the other competitors instead of watching the officials
Ask to see the review and understand every check

the_review.text: The result is confirmed. Cameras gather around you, asking how it feels to break an impossible record. You do not know yet. On your first attempt to demonstrate the solve, you drop the cube.

choices.text: Show the young competitors the mistakes you made along the way
Leave the cameras and keep the moment for yourself tonight

next_generation.text: You teach the group how to compare paths without waiting for a perfect one. The record is already being challenged, and you are glad. A hundred years was long enough for one solve to look like a law of nature.

quiet_victory.text: Alone in the hotel room, you watch Ren's recording again. This time you see not a legend but another teenager waiting for the officials. You set the cube down and let tomorrow arrive without timing it.
